grade.first_issue: The decisive claim that real-rootedness of every partial sum forces the formal power series to define an entire function is merely attributed to Pólya–Schur, without a precise statement or proof.
grade.summary: The contradiction after establishing infinite radius of convergence is correct, as is the preliminary deduction that every \(c_k\neq0\). However, the asserted entire-function theorem contains essentially the whole difficult step and is neither standard enough for an Olympiad proof nor justified here. Proving the needed coefficient decay requires a substantive root/coefficient inequality such as the one in the reference solution.
strengths: Correctly reduces the problem to nonzero coefficients and derives the final contradiction from coefficient decay.
The overall contradiction strategy is mathematically coherent.

errors.description: An unproved, specialized Pólya–Schur assertion replaces the load-bearing argument that the real-rooted partial sums impose superexponential decay on their coefficients.
